title: Earthquake: What to do
summary: Drop, Cover, Hold, and what to do after shaking stops. PLACEHOLDER — must be replaced with reviewer-approved, rights-cleared content before release (PRD §8.3, §10.3).
steps: DROP onto your hands and knees before the shaking throws you down.
Take COVER under a sturdy table or desk, protecting your head and neck. If no shelter is nearby, cover your head with your arms and stay away from glass.
HOLD ON to your shelter until the shaking stops.
If outdoors, move to an open area away from buildings, poles, and wires.
After shaking stops: expect aftershocks, check for injuries, and inspect gas, wires, and structure before moving broken items.
If your area is coastal and shaking was strong or long, move to higher ground immediately — do not wait for an official tsunami advisory.
avoid: Do not run outside while the ground is still shaking.
Do not use elevators before, during, or immediately after the shaking.
Do not stand under unsecured shelves, glass, or heavy objects that can fall.
Do not light matches or lighters until you are sure there is no gas leak.
